standard_prerequisites.name: The linearly ordered (LO) colouring of a hypergraph: a colouring in which every edge has a unique maximum colour
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Defined in the introduction of the paper, before source line 100; the counted proof recalls the equivalent form in which the minimum colour of each edge is unique
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the property that the dyadic colour assignment in the proof has to satisfy.

standard_prerequisites.name: The homogeneous system Av = 0^m attached to the edge set, and its solvability from LO 2-colourability
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the section of which the counted lemma is the first statement (source lines 240-265), where the author also notes that every coordinate of the reference solution w equals -1/3 or 2/3
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the solution u whose minimal and maximal absolute coordinate values M and m the colour bound 2 + log_2(M/m) is stated in terms of.

core_obligations: Normalise the range: rescale so that the maximal absolute value of a coordinate is M = 1, and reverse the order of the colours at the end so that it suffices to make the minimum colour of each edge unique (proof lines 273-275).
Assign the dyadic colours: give x the even colour 2l when v_x lies in (2^{-(2l+1)}, 2^{-(2l-1)}], and the odd colour 2l+1 when v_x lies in [-2^{-2l}, -2^{-(2l+2)}) (proof lines 276-281).

Verify the unique minimum on an edge: if two vertices x and y of an edge (x,y,z) receive the same even colour 2l, then the edge equation forces v_z < -2^{-2l}, so z has an odd colour strictly below 2l; the case of two equal odd colours is symmetric (proof lines 283-288).
Bound the number of colours by 2 + log_2(M/m): the range from m to M is covered by the dyadic scales used in the assignment, and the author states that this bound is immediate (proof lines 287-288).
proof_roadmap: 把解按绝对值缩放到 M=1，并把颜色顺序反过来，于是只需保证每条边的最小颜色唯一。
按 v_x 落在哪个二进区间赋偶颜色、按负值落在哪个二进区间赋奇颜色；同色两点由边方程把第三点压到更小颜色，从而唯一最小成立；颜色数由 M/m 的二进尺度给出 2+log2(M/m)。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the dyadic colouring lemma of the paper (author lemma at source lines 266-271, label lemma:unbal): any solution u of the homogeneous system Av = 0^m whose coordinates have maximal absolute value M and minimal absolute value m > 0 yields an LO colouring with 2 + log_2(M/m) colours. The proof (source lines 273-288) constructs the colouring rather than citing one: it first reduces to the equivalent requirement that the minimum colour in each edge be unique by reversing the colour order, then assigns even colours to coordinates in dyadic positive windows and odd colours to coordinates in dyadic negative windows (proof lines 276-281), and verifies the unique-minimum property by showing that two vertices of an edge sharing a colour force the third coordinate below the corresponding dyadic threshold, whence its colour is strictly smaller (proof lines 283-288). The point of the lemma is the logarithmic dependence on the ratio M/m, which is what lets the algorithm of that section spend few colours. H2.
